notes: Derived from SA-1 fixture checkov-ec2-ckv-aws-62-23893 + remediation_package #2476.

remediation_steps.step:
Back up the current Terraform file to ensure changes can be reverted if necessary.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: Backing up the file allows for easy rollback in case of errors during the remediation process.

Edit the IAM policy in the Terraform file to replace wildcard actions with specific actions.

Command:
    sed -i 's/"Action": "s3:ListBucket"/"Action": "s3:GetObject"/' /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf

Why: Replacing wildcard actions with specific actions reduces the risk of unauthorized access by adhering to the principle of least privilege.

Run Terraform plan to preview the changes and ensure they are correct before applying.

Command:
    cd /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode

Why: Terraform plan allows you to verify that the changes will be applied as intended without any errors.

Apply the changes using Terraform to update the IAM policy.

Command:
    terraform apply -auto-approve

Why: Applying the changes updates the IAM policy to enforce the least privilege principle.

Verify the IAM policy changes by checking the policy version.

Command:
    POLICY_ARN=$(terraform state show aws_iam_policy.vulnerable_policy | awk -F'"' '/arn:aws:iam::/{print $2; exit}') && aws iam get-policy-version --policy-arn "$POLICY_ARN" --version-id v1

Why: Verifying the policy ensures that the changes have been applied correctly and the policy adheres to the least privilege principle.

Re-scan with Checkov to confirm that the IAM policy no longer fails the CKV_AWS_62 check.

Command:
    checkov -d /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/ --check CKV_AWS_62 --output json --quiet --compact

Why: Re-scanning with Checkov provides authoritative proof that the vulnerability has been remediated.
